references.text: God tells Adam that he is dust and shall return to dust, which forms the basis for Abraham's recognition of being 'dust and ashes'.
Job repents in 'dust and ashes' – exactly the same expression Abraham uses to describe his own insignificance before God.
David's humility and recognition of his smallness before God reflect Abraham's humility when he speaks to the Lord.
The people of Israel acknowledge their own sinfulness and uncleanness, paralleling Abraham's recognition of being 'dust and ashes' before God.
God knows that we are dust – a recognition that reflects Abraham's humble self-description as 'dust and ashes'.
The Roman officer's acknowledgment that he is not worthy mirrors Abraham's humility when he addresses the Lord.
The tax collector who did not dare to lift his eyes to heaven but prayed for mercy shows the same kind of humility that Abraham expresses.
Theological parallel: The use of 'ashes' as a symbol of human humility and the nature of prayer.
